summary:
[  edit  ]
The LTC Out  CHOP  outputs "linear timecode" which is a SMPTE timecode data encoded into an audio signal. See also  Linear Timecode .
Use an  Info CHOP  to determine which values are currently being output.
The output of this  CHOP  can be sent to an  Audio Device Out CHOP .
See also:  LTC In CHOP

parameters.label: Play Mode
parameters.name: playmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies the method used to output LTC, there are 2 options.

parameters.label: Sequential
parameters.name: sequential
parameters.description: This mode continually plays forward.

parameters.label: Timecode  Object / CHOP / DAT
parameters.name: timecodeop
parameters.description: This mode allows the user to set the LTC value by reference to a timecode in the form of either a  CHOP ,  DAT , or  Timecode Class  object.

parameters.label: Play
parameters.name: play
parameters.description: Specifies whether the count should increment or hold steady.

parameters.label: Cue
parameters.name: cue
parameters.description: While set to on, the output is held at the specified initial values below.

parameters.label: Cue  Pulse
parameters.name: cuepulse
parameters.description: When pulsed, the output is set to the initial values below.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.name: frame
parameters.description: The initial frame to count from.

parameters.label: Second
parameters.name: second
parameters.description: The initial second to count from.

parameters.label: Minute
parameters.name: minute
parameters.description: The initial minute to count from.

parameters.label: Hour
parameters.name: hour
parameters.description: The initial hour to count from.

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.name: framerate
parameters.description: The number of complete frame messages per second the signal encodes. It is usually between 24 and 30. Note that although we support framerates above 30, using custom usage of the User Bits 1 field, the generated LTC signal is non-standard and will likely not be readable by other software or devices. LTC is limited to 30fps when following the standard.

parameters.label: Drop Frame Numbering
parameters.name: dropframe
parameters.description: Drop frame numbering converts 30 fps time code to the 29.97 fps NTSC standard. Frame numbers 0 and 1 are skipped during the first second of every minute, except multiples of 10 minutes.

parameters.label: High  FPS  Behaviour
parameters.name: highfpsbehaviour
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies the method for counting frame numbers when the set frame rate is higher than the LTC frame rate. Menu enabled only when the set frame rate is a multiple of the LTC frame rate. This menu has 2 options.

parameters.label: Cycle Frames
parameters.name: cycleframes
parameters.description: This mode loops the LTC frame count until the end of each  FPS  cycle

parameters.label: Duplicate Frames
parameters.name: duplicateframes
parameters.description: This mode repeats each individual LTC frame count in multiples until the end of each  FPS  cycle

parameters.label: Timecode  Object / CHOP / DAT
parameters.name: timecodeop
parameters.description: Set the LTC output value with a reference to a timecode. Should be a reference to either a  CHOP  with channels 'hour', 'second', 'minute', 'frame', a  DAT  with a timecode string in its first cell, or a  Timecode Class  object.

parameters.label: Audio Rate
parameters.name: audiorate
parameters.description: This audio sampling rate of the output signal.

parameters.label: User Data 1
parameters.name: user1
parameters.description: Send this value in the bits reserved for User Data 1.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table

parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: cook_frame

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time

parameters.label: warnings

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.label: The term "Frame" is a measurement of time used (1) in the  Timeline , (2) as a time
parameters.description: unit in CHOPs, and (3) as a time unit in movie files that are read into  TOPs  and written out from TOPs. The frame rate is the frames per second ( FPS ).
